text:
Lena (product): quick heads-up 1: our Private/VPC setup wizardnetworking step is getting flagged in user tests as intimidating. lots of red Xs and long rule text. can we make it feel friendlier without losing clarity?

Diego (design): agree. two ideas: 1) condensed status list with one-line explanations; 2) progressive disclosure for advanced rules (collapse by default). example one-line: 'Outbound HTTPS (443) to api.redwood.ai used to download images and updates.'

Hannah (frontend): condensed list is doable. suggest visual pattern: left status icon (green/amber/red), middle concise label + helper, right action button (Retry / Show details). keyboard: action buttons must be reachable via tab order.

Priya (a11y): please avoid color-only status. include textual status and aria-labels like aria-live region that says: 'Rule: Outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.ai  failed. Suggested action: allow outbound 443'. Also add skip-link to jump to first failing check.

Marcus (pm): user-facing copy request: make it explicit we do non-invasive probes and will not open ports or change firewall rules. Short line near the top, bold. e.g., 'We only run read-only checks from your agent; no inbound firewall changes will be made.'

Diego (design): love that. also proposing microcopy for actions: Retry -> 'Re-run check' (less technical), Details -> 'Why this matters' so users know impact.

Hannah (frontend): small implementation detail: the 'Show details' panel should include a short repro command for infra teams, but hidden by default. e.g.:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai:443/health
```
This gives ops something to share with their network team.

Priya (a11y): ok but mark code blocks with role="region" and aria-label="Diagnostic command". screen reader users should be able to expand/collapse the code and copy it. Provide a button that says 'Copy command' with aria-live confirmation 'copied'.

Lena (product): decision draft: 1) one-line compact status rows; 2) advanced/technical rules collapsed; 3) top-level bold reassurance about non-invasive checks; 4) aria-live updates + skip-link; 5) include copyable repro command in details. everyone ok?

Diego (design): ok I'll update Figma and add a compact token to component variants.

Hannah (frontend): ok I'll prototype the tab order and aria-live. will open a PR from feature/wizard-compact-status.

Priya (a11y): ok will produce a short QA checklist: VoiceOver, NVDA, keyboard-only, screen magnifier. also test with long rule lists (50+).

Marcus (pm): ok adding to sprint board under "Private onboarding UX" and tagging infra-eng for validation. please include analytics event: onboarding.network_check.fail with reason codes.

ci-bot: CI pipeline for branch feature/wizard-compact-status started (build 2489). :gear:

Lena (product): thanks team. follow-up: can we make the status rows a bit more positive in tone? e.g., 'Looks good' vs 'Pass' where appropriate. small touch but testers reacted to it.

Diego (design): noted. will use friendlier verbs.

Hannah (frontend): noted. will map status strings to i18n keys: onboarding.rules.status.good, onboarding.rules.status.issue.

ci-bot: Build 2489 passed unit tests. :white_check_mark:

Lena (product): scheduling a quick follow-up review tomorrow 9:30am. invite sent. :calendar:
